title: Organizational and project ecosystems
blurb: Tell the organizational ecosystem from the project ecosystem, and say who looks after the relationships in and between them.
question: A hospital trust and an external software supplier set up a temporary team to deliver a new patient-transfer system. Which ecosystem is that temporary team, and which ecosystem do the trust and the supplier belong to?

teach.body: Formally, the organizational ecosystem is the set of existing organizations involved (business, users and suppliers), each with its own structures, governance, culture and people. The project ecosystem is the temporary set of people, relationships, structures and ways of working created for the project. In plain English: the organizational ecosystem was there before the project and stays afterwards; the project ecosystem is the temporary 'team world' built to make the change.

rows.label: Lifespan
values: Formed for the project, then ends

teach.caption: The project ecosystem sits where the business, user and supplier interests meet (the three project interests).
Where the three interests intersect, PRINCE2 builds the project ecosystem: the temporary organization that delivers the change.

teach.body: The project ecosystem is temporary and cuts across the boundaries of established organizations, each with its own governance and culture. A temporary leader finds authority harder to exercise, and team members may be more senior than the project manager. Leading across those boundaries needs cultural intelligence: the ability to relate and work across cultures within the organizational ecosystem.

teach.body: Hollinsbrook Hospitals Trust and Larchway Software agree a project to replace paper patient-transfer forms. Project manager Tomasz Wilk builds a team of ward nurses, porters and Larchway developers. The trust and Larchway, with their own rules and cultures, are the organizational ecosystem. Tomasz's temporary team, its meetings and agreed ways of working form the project ecosystem. The board, chaired by executive Ruth Adeyemi, manages the interface with both organizations; Tomasz manages relationships inside the team.

teach.text: The business layer (which commissions the project and appoints the executive) belongs to the organizational ecosystem and sits outside the project management team. The project board is inside the project, at the directing level. Do not confuse 'the business' with 'the board'.

rows.label: The supplier company and its HR rules

teach.note: Ask: did this exist before the project, or was it created for it?

items: Organizational ecosystem: existing business, user and supplier organizations with their own structures, governance, culture and people.
Project ecosystem: the temporary people, relationships, structures and ways of working created for the project.
The project ecosystem forms where the three project interests (business, user, supplier) meet.
Board: relationships at the interface of the two ecosystems. PM: relationships within the project ecosystem.
Leading across organizational boundaries needs cultural intelligence (manual 3.3.1).
The organizing practice's design technique starts by understanding the organizational ecosystem and ends by transitioning the project back into it (manual 6.3.1).

summary: You can now define the organizational and project ecosystems and tell them apart by asking whether something existed before the project or was created for it. You can also say that the board manages the interface between them and the project manager manages relationships within the project ecosystem.

A.q: Which statement describes the project ecosystem?
options: The existing organizations involved, each with its own structures and governance
The commissioning level that appoints the executive
The temporary people, relationships and structures set up for the project
The environmental surroundings affected by the project's products
A.why: The project ecosystem is the temporary set of people, relationships, structures and ways of working created for the project (manual 3.1).

whyNot.0: That describes the organizational ecosystem, which exists before and after the project.
whyNot.1: That is the business layer, which sits in the organizational ecosystem outside the project management team.
whyNot.3: 'Ecosystem' in the people element is about people and organizations; environmental impact is handled through sustainability.

A.q: Identify the missing word in the following sentence. The [?] ecosystem is made up of the existing business, user and supplier organizations, each with its own structures, governance, culture and people.
options: project
organizational
commissioning
delivery
A.why: The organizational ecosystem is the set of existing organizations (business, users, suppliers) with their own structures, governance, culture and people (manual 3.1).

whyNot.0: The project ecosystem is the temporary set-up created for the project, not the existing organizations.
whyNot.2: Commissioning is what the business layer does (mandate, appointing the executive); PRINCE2 does not call the existing organizations a commissioning ecosystem.
whyNot.3: Delivering is one of the four organizational levels (team managers and members), not an ecosystem.

A.q: Which role is responsible for managing relationships at the interface between the organizational ecosystem and the project ecosystem?
options: Project manager
Team manager
Project support
Project board
A.why: The project board manages relationships at the interface of the organizational and project ecosystems, and supports social cohesion within the project ecosystem.

whyNot.0: The project manager manages relationships within the project ecosystem, including with the board and assurance.
whyNot.1: Team managers manage relationships within their team and its interfaces, co-creating with others in the project.
whyNot.2: Project support provides administrative and planning services; it does not manage the interface between ecosystems.

B.q: Which statement about the organizational ecosystem is correct?
options: It is created during initiation and disbanded during closure
It is limited to the people who hold roles on the project
It is defined by the project management team structure
It exists before the project starts and continues after it closes
B.why: The organizational ecosystem is the existing set of organizations; the project changes it, but it was there before and remains afterwards.

whyNot.0: Being created for the project and ending with it describes the project ecosystem.
whyNot.1: Project roles belong to the project management team; the organizational ecosystem includes the wider existing organizations.
whyNot.2: The project management team structure sets out project roles; it describes part of the project, not the existing organizations.

B.q: Which relationships is the project manager responsible for managing?
options: Those at the interface with the organizational ecosystem
Those within the project ecosystem, including the board
Those between the business layer and its other projects
Those inside each supplier's own departments
B.why: The project manager manages relationships within the project ecosystem, including with the project board and project assurance.

whyNot.0: The interface between the two ecosystems is the project board's responsibility.
whyNot.2: Relationships across the business layer's other work sit outside this project's management team.
whyNot.3: A supplier's internal departments are part of its own organization; the PM manages relationships within the project.

B.q:
Which two statements about ecosystems are correct?
1. The project ecosystem is temporary.
2. The project ecosystem forms where business, user and supplier interests meet.
3. The organizational ecosystem is created by the project board during initiation.
4. Every organization in the organizational ecosystem shares one common culture.
options: 1 and 2
1 and 3
2 and 4
3 and 4
B.why: The project ecosystem is a temporary set-up (1) built where the three project interests intersect (2).

whyNot.1: Statement 3 is false: the organizational ecosystem already exists; the board does not create it.
whyNot.2: Statement 4 is false: each organization has its own structures, governance and culture.
whyNot.3: Both 3 and 4 are false: the organizational ecosystem pre-exists the project, and its organizations have their own cultures.

C.q: A city council and an external software firm form a joint team to deliver a new parking app. Which statement correctly places them in the two ecosystems?
options: Both organizations are the project ecosystem; the business layer is the organizational one
The joint team is the organizational ecosystem; the two organizations are the project one
The council and the firm are the organizational ecosystem; the joint team is the project one
The council is the organizational ecosystem; the firm sits outside both under contract
C.why: The existing organizations (business, users and suppliers, including external ones) make up the organizational ecosystem; the temporary team created for the project is the project ecosystem.

whyNot.0: The two existing organizations are not temporary, so they are not the project ecosystem.
whyNot.1: This reverses the definitions: the temporary joint team is the project ecosystem.
whyNot.3: Suppliers, internal or external, are part of the organizational ecosystem; a contract does not put them outside it.

C.q: Why does leading people in the project ecosystem need a different style from leading an established business team?
options: The leader is temporary and may lead people more senior than themselves
Team members report to the project board rather than the project manager
The project ecosystem has no culture of its own that needs managing
Leadership passes to the business layer once delivery stages begin
C.why: Project teams are temporary and cross organizational boundaries, so a temporary leader finds authority harder to exercise, and team members may be more senior than the PM (manual 3.3).

whyNot.1: Team managers and members work within constraints set by the project manager, not directly for the board.
whyNot.2: A project culture does emerge, and agreed ways of working must be kept aligned with it (manual 3.2.3).
whyNot.3: The business layer commissions the project and sits outside it; it does not take over leadership during delivery.

C.q: Where does the business layer that commissions a project sit?
options: At the directing level of the project management team
In the organizational ecosystem, outside the project team
In the project ecosystem, above the project board
At the delivering level, alongside the team managers
C.why: The business layer is part of the existing organization: it provides the mandate and appoints the executive, and sits outside the project management team.

whyNot.0: The directing level is the project board, which is inside the project management team.
whyNot.2: The business layer is not created for the project, so it is not part of the temporary project ecosystem.
whyNot.3: The delivering level is team managers and team members, who are inside the project.

reteach.title: The building and the scaffolding
reteach.question: Picture a building having an extension added. What is permanent, and what is put up only to do the work?

blocks.body: The existing building, with its owners, tenants and rules, is like the organizational ecosystem: it was there first and stays. The scaffolding and site crew put up for the extension are like the project ecosystem: built for the job, with their own ways of working, and taken down when the job is done. The building is different afterwards, just as business as usual resumes in a new form.

blocks.text: Test yourself with one question: was it created for this project? If yes, it belongs to the project ecosystem. If it existed already (including suppliers and the business layer), it belongs to the organizational ecosystem.

explain.body: The existing organizations involved in or touched by the project: the business, users and suppliers. Each has its own structures, governance, culture and people, and each continues after the project ends.

test.q: An external supplier's company, with its own HR policies and culture, provides developers for a project. Which ecosystem is the supplier company part of?
options: The project ecosystem
The organizational ecosystem
The project management team
The commissioning business layer
test.why: Suppliers, internal or external, are existing organizations with their own governance and culture, so they are part of the organizational ecosystem.

whyNot.0: The project ecosystem is the temporary set-up created for the project, not the supplier's company.
whyNot.2: The project management team is the set of project roles; the supplier's company as a whole is an existing organization.
whyNot.3: The business layer is the commissioning part of the business, not an external supplier.

explain.body: The temporary set of people, relationships, structures and ways of working created to deliver the project. It forms where the business, user and supplier interests intersect, and it ends when the project closes.

test.q: Which is part of the project ecosystem?
options: The user department's long-standing routines
The supplier's company governance rules
The ways of working agreed for the project team
The business layer's strategy and portfolio
test.why: Ways of working agreed for the project are part of the temporary project ecosystem.

whyNot.0: Long-standing routines existed before the project, so they belong to the organizational ecosystem.
whyNot.1: A supplier's own governance belongs to that existing organization.
whyNot.3: The business layer's strategy belongs to the existing organization outside the project.

explain.body: The project board manages relationships at the interface between the organizational and project ecosystems and supports social cohesion in the project. The project manager manages relationships within the project ecosystem, including with the board and assurance.

test.q: Which responsibility belongs to the project board?
options: Supporting social cohesion in the project ecosystem
Producing checkpoint reports for the project manager
Maintaining the registers held in the project log
Setting the tolerances for each team's work package
test.why: The project board monitors and supports social cohesion within the project ecosystem and manages the interface between the ecosystems.

whyNot.1: Checkpoint reports are produced by team managers for the project manager.
whyNot.2: Maintaining registers is a project support task under the project manager.
whyNot.3: Work package tolerances are set by the project manager.

explain.body: Because the project ecosystem spans several organizations, leaders often guide people who do not report to them. This needs cultural intelligence: the ability to relate and work across cultures within the organizational ecosystem (manual 3.3.1).

test.q: What is cultural intelligence, as used in PRINCE2's people element?
options: The board's set of shared values and rules for governing decisions
The skill of writing a separate role description for each culture
The ability to relate and work across cultures in the ecosystem
The analysis of attitudes recorded in the risk register
test.why: Cultural intelligence is the capability to relate and work across cultures within the organizational ecosystem (manual 3.3.1).

whyNot.0: Setting rules and shared values is a board governance responsibility, not cultural intelligence.
whyNot.1: Role descriptions should reflect capability, authority and availability; that is not what cultural intelligence means.
whyNot.3: The risk register records specific risks; it is not a measure of cultural intelligence.
